name: VS 61 SR CDF - Spectrally Selective
shortDescription: At 61% VLT, VS 61 is Vista's lightest SpectraSelect film for near-invisible solar control on historic glass.
description:
VS 61 SR CDF is the lightest Vista SpectraSelect option in this Philadelphia catalog, built for projects where visible change to the glass is the first concern. Its 61% visible light transmission keeps rooms bright, while spectrally selective technology targets infrared heat more than daylight. Because the construction is non-metallized, it also avoids the RF and cellular interference questions that can come with metal-based solar films.

That makes VS 61 especially useful on Society Hill brownstones, historic district facades, condominium associations, and storefronts where review boards or ownership rules leave almost no tolerance for a noticeable tint. It is the film to consider when the building needs relief from afternoon heat but the windows still need to read as original, clear architectural glass from the street. That is a common concern on divided-lite windows, older sash, and prominent front elevations where even a small visual shift can create objections before performance is considered.

In practical terms, 61% VLT means more than half of visible daylight still passes through the window, while the film rejects up to 49% of solar heat and blocks over 99% of UV. The low-reflectance appearance helps preserve exterior character, and the infrared-focused performance supports comfort without relying on a mirrored surface. Compatibility still depends on glass type, orientation, and insulated-glass details.

Choose VS 61 when the project values daylight and appearance above maximum glare control. VS 60 is a close alternative when a slightly firmer specification is acceptable, while V 58, V 45, and the 33% films step progressively into more visible tint and stronger light management. VS 61 is the preservation-sensitive starting point of the lineup.

name: VS 60 SR CDF - Spectrally Selective
shortDescription: VS 60 gives historic Philadelphia glass a slightly firmer SpectraSelect spec while staying almost clear.
description:
VS 60 SR CDF sits just below VS 61 in the Vista SpectraSelect family, with a 60% visible light transmission that remains bright and restrained. The difference is subtle, but useful: it gives specifiers one more step of solar control when the lightest film feels too marginal, while still keeping the non-metallized, low-reflectance character that defines SpectraSelect.

In Philadelphia, that small shift matters on Society Hill, Old City, Queen Village, and Chestnut Hill properties where glass appearance is scrutinized but summer sun still creates comfort problems. It also fits professional offices, hotels, and schools that need product documentation for facilities teams without giving the building a reflective commercial look from the sidewalk. The product is also easy to sample beside original trim, stone, and brick because the finished glass does not announce itself as a design change.

The specs place VS 60 at 60% VLT, up to 49% heat rejection, and over 99% UV block. Like the rest of the SpectraSelect range, it is designed to reject infrared heat without a metal layer, so Wi-Fi, cellular, radio, and building access systems are not the tradeoff. The finished appearance is near clear, with enough performance to make a measurable difference on sun-exposed glass.

Choose VS 60 when VS 61 is visually ideal but the project needs a touch more confidence in the solar-control specification. V 58 becomes the next step when a barely noticeable neutral tint is acceptable, while V 45 and the 33% films are better for glare and privacy. VS 60 is the quiet middle point for appearance-first Philadelphia work.

shortDescription: V 58 adds a barely visible neutral tint for clients who want more control than VS 60 but a clean facade.

V 58 SR CDF - Neutral is the first SpectraSelect option in this set that begins to look intentionally specified rather than nearly invisible. At 58% VLT, it still preserves generous daylight, but the neutral tone gives the glass a cleaner, more managed appearance than the ultra-clear VS 61 and VS 60 films. It avoids the bronze or cool gray cast that can distract from masonry or modern curtain wall design.

That makes V 58 a good fit for Philadelphia clients who want a small privacy and glare improvement without changing the personality of the building. It works on Center City offices, Old City boutique hospitality glass, historic rowhomes with enlarged rear windows, and mixed-use storefronts where a subtle, professional finish is more appropriate than a darker privacy film. This is also a useful choice when owners want the glass to look a little more finished in daylight but still avoid a strong privacy-film signal.

The film pairs 58% visible light transmission with up to 49% heat rejection and over 99% UV block. The neutral, low-reflectance appearance helps maintain clear views and a balanced interior color temperature. Its solar performance is strongest where the goal is steady comfort, reduced fading, and less heat build-up rather than dramatic darkening. Glass review remains important on insulated units and intense south or west exposures.

Choose V 58 when VS 60 still feels too transparent for the design brief, but V 45 would be more tint than the facade can carry. It is the stepping-stone SpectraSelect film: more apparent than the lightest products, less assertive than the midrange neutral and 33% options, and especially useful when exterior appearance has to stay composed.

name: V 38 SR PS8 - Safety - Dual Reflective
shortDescription: V 38 PS8 combines 38% dual reflective privacy with 8 mil construction for public-facing glass.
description:
V 38 SR PS8 combines dual reflective solar performance with an 8 mil safety construction. That makes it distinct from standard V 38 SR CDF: it manages heat, glare, and daytime privacy while also helping retain glass fragments after impact. It is a two-in-one specification for projects that need solar control and a stronger glass-retention layer.

In Philadelphia, V 38 PS8 fits ground-floor retail, lobby glass, public-facing offices, healthcare entries, and school or campus windows where visibility, comfort, and risk reduction all matter. It is especially useful when the client wants daytime privacy but cannot ignore breakage behavior on glass close to sidewalks, entrances, or transit-adjacent foot traffic. Frames, attachment methods, existing glass strength, and the size of each lite still shape the final recommendation, especially on doors and large storefront panes. It also keeps the visual character close to the standard V 38 dual reflective product, which helps when privacy and safety goals share the same elevation.

The specs include 38% VLT, up to 61% heat rejection, over 99% UV block, and 8 mil thickness. The dual reflective finish gives a moderate exterior presence and lower interior reflectance for better night views. The safety layer helps retain glass fragments and can delay forced entry through broken glass as one part of a broader glass, frame, and attachment strategy.

Choose V 38 PS8 when the project needs the balanced privacy level of V 38 plus fragment retention. V 28 PS8 is darker and more privacy-forward for higher-risk or brighter exposures. Standard V 38 SR CDF is appropriate when safety construction is not part of the scope. V 38 PS8 is the moderate safety-plus-solar option.

Choose Ceramic 35 when the exposure is demanding and comfort matters more than maximum daylight. Ceramic 45 is the better compromise if the room needs a brighter feel, Ceramic 55 is the balanced commercial option, and Ceramic 65 is for daylight-first spaces. Ceramic 35 is Vista's ceramic answer for Philadelphia glass that takes the hardest sun.

It is also useful for street-facing residential windows when occupants want more separation from sidewalk traffic without choosing a very dark film. The result is a film that can serve both tenant comfort and storefront presentation, especially where people work or gather close to the glass. It also gives owners a clear upgrade path from subtle privacy to stronger privacy without immediately changing the entire feel of the room.

The specs are 38% VLT, up to 61% heat rejection, and over 99% UV block. The blue-gray dual reflective appearance helps reduce glare and solar heat, and the lower interior reflectance improves night-view comfort compared with one-way mirror style films. The tradeoff is that the exterior appearance will be noticeable, especially in direct daylight.

Choose V 38 when V 48 is too subtle and V 28 would be too dark for the room or facade. It is the practical center of the dual reflective range: enough privacy to change how the glass performs at street level, but enough daylight and view quality to keep interiors comfortable through a full Philadelphia workday.

SpectraSelect films are better for appearance-sensitive infrared rejection, ceramic films are premium non-metal solar choices, and dual reflective films focus on privacy. VE 50 is the Vista option with the clearest year-round payback story for Philadelphia rowhomes and older glass.

name: V 48 SR CDF - Dual Reflective
shortDescription: V 48 is Vista's lightest dual reflective film for subtle daytime privacy and clear interior views.
description:
V 48 SR CDF is the lightest dual reflective Vista film in this catalog, designed for clients who want a mild daytime privacy upgrade without making the room feel dark. Its exterior reflectance is subtle compared with the darker dual reflective products, while the lower interior reflectance helps preserve usable views from inside, including after dark.

That makes V 48 a good match for Fishtown rowhomes, Northern Liberties lofts, boutique offices, and street-facing living rooms where occupants want a little more separation from the sidewalk. It can also work on storefront or hospitality glass when the goal is a polished exterior finish rather than a strong mirror effect. It is especially helpful where people want the psychological comfort of less exposure without making the room feel closed down during the day. That restraint is useful on residential blocks where occupants want less exposure but neighbors and associations still care about facade consistency.

At 48% VLT, the film remains relatively bright while rejecting up to 55% solar heat and blocking over 99% UV. Dual reflective construction means the film is more reflective to the outside than to the inside, a key distinction from standard reflective films that can feel mirror-like at night from within the room. The appearance is still more visible than SpectraSelect or ceramic films.

Choose V 48 when privacy is secondary to daylight and view quality. V 38 creates a more noticeable exterior presence, V 28 is a stronger privacy film, and V 18 or V 14 are for assertive street-facing control. V 48 is the softest entry into Vista's dual reflective lineup for Philadelphia buildings.

benefits.heading: Daytime Privacy
benefits.body: V 48 SR CDF - Dual Reflective increases exterior reflectance in daylight, helping street-facing Philadelphia glass feel more private without blocking the view from inside.

benefits.heading: Night View Balance
benefits.body: Lower interior reflectance makes the room less mirror-like after dark than standard reflective films, a practical difference in high-rise and restaurant glass.

benefits.heading: Solar Glare Control
benefits.body: At 48% VLT, it cuts visible glare and rejects solar heat for conference rooms, storefronts, and west-facing facades.

name: V 45 SR CDF - Neutral
shortDescription: V 45 is the balanced neutral SpectraSelect choice for office towers, labs, and glare-prone glass.
description:
V 45 SR CDF - Neutral is the middle ground of the Vista SpectraSelect neutral lineup. Its 45% visible light transmission creates a noticeable solar-control finish, but the look remains quiet and architectural rather than shiny or dark. For many Philadelphia commercial projects, it is the point where comfort, glare reduction, and facade restraint line up cleanly.

This film fits University City lab buildings, Center City office towers, institutional suites, and conference rooms where large glass areas bring heat and screen glare into the workday. It can also make sense for residential towers near Rittenhouse Square or Logan Square when occupants want a more comfortable room without making the windows read as heavy privacy glass from outside. It is also a practical sample for tenant improvement projects, because the change is visible enough to evaluate without overwhelming the existing design.

Technically, V 45 combines 45% VLT with up to 61% heat rejection and over 99% UV block. The neutral tone helps avoid the color shift that can happen with bronze or strongly gray films, while the spectrally selective construction improves comfort without relying on metal. Expect a clear reduction in brightness compared with V 58, but still enough daylight for offices, labs, and living spaces that depend on natural light.

Choose V 45 when the lightest SpectraSelect products are too subtle and the 33% films would feel too dark or privacy-oriented. V 58 is softer; V 33 SR adds stronger glare control; V 33 BR adds warmth. V 45 is the practical midrange specification for Philadelphia glass that needs performance but still has to look refined.

name: V 33 SR CDF - Neutral
shortDescription: V 33 SR is the stronger neutral SpectraSelect option for Center City glass taking afternoon heat.
description:
V 33 SR CDF - Neutral is the standard gray-neutral 33% film in the Vista SpectraSelect group. It is designed for clients who have moved past subtle heat control and need a more definite reduction in brightness, glare, and solar gain. The tone stays clean and architectural, but the tint is clearly present on the glass.

In Philadelphia, V 33 is a strong fit for south- and west-facing Center City offices, conference rooms, residential tower units, and storefront interiors where afternoon sun overwhelms HVAC and screens. It also works on commercial glass where the owner wants a calm, consistent appearance across a facade without the warmer bronze personality of V 33 BR. The film can make meeting rooms, workstations, and upper-floor residential spaces feel calmer during peak sun without introducing a warm bronze tone.

The 33% VLT level transmits less daylight than V 45, while rejecting up to 66% of solar heat and blocking over 99% UV. The result is stronger glare control, better visual comfort, and a more shaded interior feel. Because it is spectrally selective and non-metallized, it supports heat rejection without creating signal-interference concerns for offices, residences, or technology-heavy spaces.

Choose V 33 SR when V 45 is too light for the exposure and V 33 BR is too warm for the architecture. It is the darker, cleaner neutral choice in this subset, best for performance-focused projects that still want to avoid a reflective or decorative look. For maximum daylight, step back to V 58, VS 60, or VS 61.

name: VS 70 SR CDF - Spectrally Selective
shortDescription: Vista's most transparent SpectraSelect film — 70% VLT with non-metallic solar control for preservation-sensitive Philadelphia glass.
description:
VS 70 SR CDF sits at the lightest end of the Vista SpectraSelect family, designed for situations where visible tint is simply not an option. At 70% visible light transmission, it reads as nearly clear glass from any angle — yet its non-metallized spectrally selective construction still intercepts infrared heat before it enters the building. For projects where a historic commission, condo board, or corporate design standard demands glass that looks untouched, VS 70 is the film that threads that needle.

In Philadelphia's built environment, that matters on specific building types more than others. Society Hill and Old City townhomes with divided-lite sash windows, Rittenhouse Square condominium facades where HOA design rules prohibit any perceptible tint, and University City campus buildings with contemporary glazing systems that need to maintain an institutional clean look are all candidates. VS 70 lets those properties address afternoon solar gain without surfacing a visible product decision every time someone walks past the building.

The spectrally selective construction means VS 70 targets near-infrared radiation — the heat-carrying wavelengths — rather than blocking visible light indiscriminately. That gives it meaningful solar performance at a VLT level where traditional reflective or neutral films would offer little protection. UV blocking exceeds 99%, which provides the fade and skin protection benefit regardless of how light the tint reads.

Choose VS 70 when appearance constraints are the primary driver and modest solar control is enough. VS 61 and VS 60 step into progressively firmer heat rejection at slightly lower VLT, and V 58 or V 45 add visible tint for spaces that can accommodate it. VS 70 is the Vista film for projects where the answer to 'will anyone notice?' must be no.

benefits.heading: Near-Clear Appearance
benefits.body: At 70% VLT, VS 70 SR CDF is virtually indistinguishable from untreated glass — the right call for historic commissions, condo boards, and design-controlled Philadelphia facades.

benefits.heading: Non-Metallic Solar Control
benefits.body: Spectrally selective construction targets infrared heat without a metallized layer, so Wi-Fi, cellular, and building automation signals pass through unaffected.

benefits.heading: UV Defense
benefits.body: Over 99% UV block protects furnishings, flooring, and artwork in Society Hill rowhomes and Rittenhouse Square residences without any perceptible change to window appearance.

name: VE 35 SR CDF - Low-E
shortDescription: Darker Low-E option at 35% VLT — combines Vista's four-season insulating technology with daytime privacy for Philadelphia glass.
description:
VE 35 SR CDF is the lower-VLT option in Vista's Low-E line, pairing the series' signature year-round insulating performance with meaningful daytime privacy. Where VE 50 keeps a near-clear appearance, VE 35 steps into visible tint territory — 35% visible light transmission provides a noticeably darker look that reduces direct line-of-sight from outside while still transmitting substantial daylight indoors. It is the film for property owners who want the Low-E thermal story and a measure of privacy in the same product.

Philadelphia properties that benefit most are street-facing residential and ground-floor commercial spaces where both solar comfort and visual exposure are genuine concerns. A South Street retail storefront dealing with west-afternoon sun and passerby views, a Fishtown live-work rowhouse with large front windows, or a University City office with ground-floor glass facing a pedestrian corridor — each of those scenarios benefits from the privacy dimension that VE 50 does not offer. The Low-E layer continues to perform in winter, reducing heat loss through the glass and the drafty feeling that makes older Philadelphia single-pane windows uncomfortable in cold months.

At 35% VLT, VE 35 blocks a meaningful amount of glare in addition to its thermal work. The spec positions it between the near-clear Low-E comfort film and the more aggressively dark Dual Reflective options. It does not deliver the mirror-finish daytime privacy of a DR15 or DR25, but it provides passive privacy without the after-dark fishbowl effect that high-exterior-reflectance films create.

Choose VE 35 when the performance case is four-season thermal comfort but the project also needs reduced street visibility. VE 50 is the better choice when appearance must remain near-clear. The Dual Reflective series is the alternative when maximum daytime privacy outweighs the year-round insulating benefit.

benefits.heading: Four-Season Low-E Performance
benefits.body: VE 35 SR CDF - Low-E manages summer solar heat and reduces winter heat loss through Philadelphia single-pane glass — the same thermal story as VE 50, with added privacy.

benefits.heading: Daytime Privacy
benefits.body: The 35% VLT tint reduces direct line-of-sight from street level into South Street storefronts, Fishtown rowhouses, and ground-floor Philadelphia offices without a full-mirror exterior.

benefits.heading: Glare Reduction
benefits.body: Darker than VE 50, VE 35 cuts afternoon glare on south- and west-facing glass where solar exposure makes screens difficult and spaces uncomfortable during peak hours.
